original.target_description: Unresolved original target: supplied study 6 and p.3; source uses study labels 1, 2a, 2b, 3a, 3b, 4 and reports multiple relevant tests.

notes: Identity independently confirmed: canonical text is a PMC full-article parse headed Belief in free will affects causal attributions when judging others’ behavior, by Oliver Genschow, Davide Rigoni, and Marcel Brass, Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A 114(38):10071–10076 (2017), DOI 10.1073/pnas.1701916114. Includes main report and supporting-information text; it is not an abstract-only excerpt or a preregistration. No PDF was supplied, and page 3 cannot be verified from this unpaginated parse. The paper labels studies 1, 2a, 2b, 3a, 3b, and 4; there is no study explicitly labelled 6. Do not relabel Study 4 as Study 6 based on its sequence. The broad description does not select a unique outcome or test. Candidates only, not assigned values: Study 3a correspondence-bias manipulation contrast d=0.41, t=2.59, P=0.01, alongside interaction F(1,162)=6.72, P=0.01, partial eta-squared=0.04; its participant total is 164 and FWI analyses are limited to n=137. Study 3b correspondence-bias manipulation contrast d=0.19, t=2.10, P=0.036, alongside interaction F(1,502)=4.41, P=0.036, partial eta-squared=0.01; reported sample 504, with supporting information documenting replacement recruitment and 202 discarded participants. Study 4 reports 212 subjects (not established here as critical-model analytic N), a within-person internal/external attribution contrast dz=0.82, t=11.92, P<0.001, a belief/correspondence-bias correlation r=0.35, P<0.001, and distinct prescribed-behavior correlations r=0.33 overall, r=0.32 reward, r=0.27 punishment, each P<0.001, plus mediation coefficients. No conversion or N arithmetic performed. All three assigned fields remain unresolved because neither study identity nor critical test is uniquely established. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
